title: Ambedkar: Caste Annihilation and Constitutional Democracy

scenes.text: Can political freedom bring true democracy without ending caste inequality?
scenes.narration: Imagine gaining political independence, but remaining trapped in social oppression every single day. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar argued that genuine freedom is meaningless without first annihilating caste inequality.

scenes.text: A cricket team benches star players solely due to family background.
scenes.narration: Here is an everyday analogy: if a cricket team bans its finest players from batting just because of their families, the team collapses. Likewise, Ambedkar warned that caste divisions split India into warring camps, blocking real nationhood.

scenes.heading: Hierarchy of Brahmanism
scenes.narration: Here's the trick to his critique of Brahmanism. Ambedkar showed that caste is not a natural division of labour, but an artificial hierarchy. It enforces endogamy—marrying only within one's caste—and purity to keep Broken Men segregated.

scenes.heading: Gandhi versus Ambedkar on Caste
scenes.narration: Look at the clash between Gandhi and Ambedkar. While Gandhi defended Varna as functional specialization, Ambedkar insisted that real caste is a division of labourers based on birth, which must be completely destroyed.

scenes.heading: Indian Society's Basic Structure
scenes.narration: Next, see how Ambedkar tackled Karl Marx. Marx viewed economic class as the root of injustice, but Ambedkar countered that in India, the religious ideology of Brahmanism forms the real foundation of social oppression.

scenes.heading: Constitutional Democracy over Revolution
items: Reject violent revolution and proletarian dictatorship
Use state agency to cure social injustice
Protect individual dignity through liberal democracy
scenes.narration: Because society was more oppressive than the state, Ambedkar rejected violent Marxist revolution. Instead, he chose constitutional democracy, trusting state-backed affirmative action and legal rights to protect human dignity.

items: Caste is an enforced division of labourers
Brahmanical ideology forms India's core social structure
Constitutional democracy is vital for social justice
scenes.narration: Here are your key takeaways: caste is an oppressive division of labourers, ideological reform must dismantle Brahmanism, and constitutional democracy remains the true path to equal dignity.
